messages:
maria_g: quick context — SBOM scan flagged a couple of 'operator' SSH keys baked into the old base image layers (found during ephemeral operator key sweep). We need a coordinated rebuild + signing, plus an RBAC tweak so only the image-signer role can access the KMS key. can we sync timelines?

jon_d: ugh, saw that in the triage output. looks like two keys in /root/.ssh from a prebuild step that slipped through. not a runtime compromise but still counts as secrets in image. CVE mention: not a vuln, more of a secrets/provenance issue.

alex_r: important: if we rotate the cosign key to KMS-backed, we'll need to update deployer role to allow kms:Sign on the signing key for the new service account. do we want to do a temporary elevated role for the canary image push?

security_bot: [alert] SBOM scan: image: base-ubuntu:20231118 -> secrets_found: 2 (ssh_key) | scan_id: sbom-2024-11-03-4187 | link: https://ci.internal/reports/sbom-4187

maria_g: canary plan proposal: 1) create sanitized base image (drop keys, regenerate any build creds) 2) sign with KMS-backed cosign key (rotate existing key) 3) push canary tag to private registry (tag: base-ephemeral-sanitized-canary-1745) 4) run smoke + vuln scan + SBOM -> then promote. target window: today 11:30 PT.

maria_g: RBAC ask: security to suggest minimal IAM for image-signer SA. ideally: kms:AsymmetricSign for cosign key + storage:Write for registry push. nothing else.

tanya_s: oncall question — rollback plan? if canary fails, do we have automatic fallback to previous nodes? we should ensure the runtime can still pull older digests (don't delete old tags). also need a post-deploy check that audit logs capture cosign verification details.

ken_p: runtime note — while rebuilding, let's switch runtime to rootless mode for canary pods and apply stricter seccomp and drop these caps: CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_RAW, CAP_SYS_PTRACE. also enable userns remap where possible. this reduces blast radius if an image contains something unexpected.

jon_d: triage detail — reproduction: i pulled the offending image locally, inspected layers with dive, found keys in layer 7 from 'builder:copy-ssh' step. quick fix: remove that build stage and use a multi-stage build that never copies /.ssh into final image.

alex_r: k8s RBAC snippet idea (for discussion):
```yaml
kind: Role
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: image-signer
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["secrets"]
  verbs: ["get"]
# KMS is external; map via iam roles for the signer SA
```
we'll need an IAM doc update.

maria_g: audit logging: ensure that cosign verify is logged to our central audit stream (trace ID in metadata). add an annotation on the image object with signer:sha256 and audit-url. devexp pls help add to deployer docs.

devexp: can do — i'll add a short runbook snippet under docs/internal/image-signing.md and link to the audit dashboard. will include the cosign KMS instructions and RBAC Checklist.

tanya_s: also: for incident response, tag tickets `sec:image-sanitization` and attach SBOM + layer diff. that'll speed up root cause triage if this pops again.

maria_g: action items: @jon_d remove offending builder step + open PR; @alex_r prepare IAM change + PR for signer SA; @ken_p prepare seccomp + pod spec for canary; @devexp add runbook; @tanya_s prepare rollback playbook. aiming to start canary 11:30 PT. please ack. :white_check_mark:

jon_d: ack. will open PR in 15.

alex_r: ack — will draft IAM and include least-priv policy.

ken_p: ack, will push seccomp profile to git and create kustomize overlay for canary.

devexp: ack, will have runbook PR up before deploy.

security_bot: [info] ticket created: SEC-2142 "ephemeral operator key in base image" assigned to maria_g.

maria_g: thanks all — i'll kick off the rebuild after jon's PR lands. keep logs and screenshots for postmortem. if anything blocks the key rotation to KMS cosign, ping me in-thread. :rocket:
